claims.text: HEA components produced by standard laser-based powder deposition can exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
HEA components produced by standard laser-based powder deposition can exhibit high residual stresses.
HEA components produced by standard laser-based powder deposition can contain porosity and micro-cracks.
In situ substrate preheating moderates thermal gradients across the melt pool and deposited layers.
In situ substrate preheating moderates cooling rates across the melt pool and deposited layers.
Substrate preheating decreases the temperature differential between the molten material and the supporting substrate.
Decreasing the melt-to-substrate temperature differential slows the cooling rate.
Substrate preheating minimizes thermal shock during laser-based additive manufacturing.
Moderated cooling and reduced thermal shock promote more uniform microstructure formation.
Substrate preheating lowers residual stresses in additively manufactured HEA components.
Substrate preheating improves the dimensional precision of laser-additively-manufactured HEA components relative to room-temperature-substrate builds.
Substrate preheating reduces porosity and cracks relative to room-temperature-substrate builds.
Substrate preheating enhances mechanical properties relative to room-temperature-substrate builds.
Room-temperature-substrate HEA builds typically have significant dimensional inaccuracies.
Room-temperature-substrate HEA builds typically have high residual stresses and a relatively high density of fabrication-induced defects.
The proposed improvements should hold for standard HEA compositions under normal ranges of laser-deposition parameters.
The effects of substrate preheating may differ for extreme HEA compositions.
Preheat temperatures above an optimal range may cause unintended microstructural changes or phase instability.
